title: BIS third major 2024 China semiconductor package: 140 Entity List additions, new FDP rules
summary: BIS issued a package of rules to impair China's ability to produce advanced-node semiconductors: two new Foreign-Direct Product rules, 140 additions to the Entity List, and new controls on high-bandwidth memory, supercomputers, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, effective December 2, 2024. The rules extended license requirements for advanced computing items to any worldwide destination meeting certain criteria, forming the regulatory baseline the Biden AI Diffusion Rule (January 2025) and subsequent Trump-era actions built on.
source_name: Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) -- Commerce Strengthens Export Controls to Restrict China's Capability to Produce Advanced Semiconductors for Military Applications

title: Biden Administration issues the AI Diffusion Rule
summary: BIS issued a worldwide licensing framework for advanced semiconductors and AI computing commodities, sorting nearly every country into a small number of access tiers. Enforcement was set to begin 15 May 2025.
source_name: O'Melveny -- Trump Administration Modifies Direction of Regulating AI Chips

title: Chip Security Act companion bill (S. 1705) introduced in the Senate
countries: United States (export-control implications for all 17 tracked countries)
summary: Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR) introduced the Senate companion to the House Chip Security Act, requiring the Secretary of Commerce to issue standards for location-verification mechanisms on advanced integrated-circuit products to detect and deter diversion to unauthorized destinations.
source_name: Congress.gov -- S.1705, Chip Security Act (119th Congress)

title: Trump Administration rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule
summary: BIS announced rescission of the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule days before its enforcement date, citing over-complexity and diplomatic friction. This reopened the door to the bilateral, entity-specific dealmaking that produced the HUMAIN and UAE authorizations later in 2025 and 2026.
source_name: TechCrunch -- Trump administration officially rescinds Biden's AI diffusion rules

title: Nvidia agrees to supply Saudi Arabia's Humain with 18,000 GB300 Blackwell chips
summary: During President Trump's Gulf trip, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced Nvidia would ship over 18,000 GB300 Blackwell AI chips to Saudi AI venture Humain for a 500-megawatt data-center buildout, with several hundred thousand more chips planned over five years -- a deal enabled by the Trump administration's shift away from the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule (formally rescinded the same week).
source_name: CNBC -- Nvidia sending 18,000 of its top AI chips to Saudi Arabia

title: Chip Security Act (H.R. 3447) introduced in the House
countries: United States (export-control implications for all 8 tracked countries)
summary: Reps. Bill Huizenga (R-MI) and Bill Foster (D-IL) introduced bipartisan legislation requiring advanced AI chips to carry location-verification mechanisms to detect and prevent diversion to unauthorized countries and end users.

title: BIS final rule substantially relaxes export controls on Syria
summary: Following President Trump's June 2025 executive order revoking comprehensive Syria sanctions, BIS issued a final rule easing Export Administration Regulations controls on Syria, removing license requirements for most civilian-use U.S.-origin goods, software, and technology and facilitating license approvals for telecommunications, power, and civil-aviation-related exports.
source_name: Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) -- Commerce Eases Export Controls on Syria

title: Senate passes GAIN AI Act as an amendment to the FY2026 NDAA
countries: United States (export-control implications for all 17 tracked countries)
summary: The Senate adopted Sen. Jim Banks and Sen. Elizabeth Warren's Guaranteeing Access and Innovation for National AI (GAIN AI) Act as an amendment to the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, requiring chipmakers to fully satisfy U.S. customer orders -- and requiring export licenses to arms-embargoed and comprehensively sanctioned countries, including Iran and Syria -- before prioritizing sales abroad.
source_name: Nextgov/FCW -- AI export control bill passes Senate as NDAA amendment

title: BIS issues first Nvidia AI-chip export licenses to the UAE under the AI Acceleration Partnership
summary: BIS issued Nvidia's first export licenses for advanced AI chips destined for the UAE since the start of the Trump administration, granted under the US-UAE AI Acceleration Partnership signed during Trump's May 2025 visit and reported as worth several billion dollars -- enabling initial GPU shipments toward the Stargate UAE data-center project.
source_name: DataCenterDynamics -- Department of Commerce issues export licenses for Nvidia chips destined for the UAE

title: GAIN AI Act of 2025 (S. 3150) introduced as standalone Senate bill
countries: United States (export-control implications for all 17 tracked countries)
summary: Sen. Jim Banks, with bipartisan cosponsors including Sens. Warren, Cotton, Schumer, McCormick, and Coons, introduced the standalone GAIN AI Act of 2025, requiring exporters of advanced AI chips to certify that U.S. purchasers' demand is met before chips can be sold to licensees in countries of concern, including arms-embargoed and comprehensively sanctioned destinations.
source_name: Congress.gov -- S.3150, GAIN AI Act of 2025 (119th Congress)

title: Saudi HUMAIN and UAE G42 authorized for capped advanced-chip purchases
summary: Commerce authorized HUMAIN (Saudi Arabia) and G42 (UAE) to each purchase up to the equivalent of 35,000 Nvidia GB300-class accelerators, subject to security and reporting conditions and BIS compliance monitoring -- capped and entity-specific, not a country-wide rule.
source_name: Vision2030.ai -- US Chip Export Controls: Saudi-UAE Divergence

title: DOJ Operation Gatekeeper dismantles $160m AI-chip-smuggling network to China
summary: DOJ announced the takedown of a China-linked smuggling network that moved at least $160 million in export-controlled Nvidia H100 and H200 GPUs out of the United States using straw purchasers and rebranding schemes; a Texas-based operator pleaded guilty and roughly $50 million in GPUs were seized, with two additional defendants charged.
source_name: U.S. Department of Justice -- Office of Public Affairs, U.S. Authorities Shut Down Major China-Linked AI Tech Smuggling Network

title: DOJ unseals $2.5bn AI-chip-smuggling indictment linked to Super Micro
summary: Three men connected to server manufacturer Super Micro were indicted for conspiring to illegally ship AI servers containing Nvidia chips worth $2.5bn to Chinese customers between 2024-2025, allegedly rerouted through a Southeast Asian intermediary.
source_name: U.S. Department of Justice -- Office of Public Affairs press release

title: Second chip-smuggling case: Thailand-routed diversion scheme
summary: A Hong Kong national and two US citizens were arrested following an FBI investigation for ordering roughly 750 servers worth ~$170m and signing false certifications that the equipment was not destined for China.
source_name: Eastern Herald -- US Exposes Massive AI Chip Smuggling Network to China

title: House Foreign Affairs Committee marks up the Chip Security Act
countries: United States (export-control implications for all 8 tracked countries)
summary: The committee advanced H.R. 3447 toward a full House vote, roughly ten months after introduction and one week after the Super Micro-linked smuggling indictment -- the enforcement case is widely read as having accelerated the bill's committee movement.
source_name: FDD Action -- Support H.R. 3447, the Chip Security Act, and Other Measures

title: UAE upgraded to BIS Country Group A:5, removed from D:3/D:4
summary: BIS moved the UAE into Country Group A:5 and named G42, Core42, and eight US AI firms as approved end users eligible for license-free advanced-chip access under a new Advanced Computing Items exception -- the most favorable export-control status of any country in this tracker, though still entity-specific rather than unconditional.
source_name: Steptoe -- Commerce Upgrades the UAE to Favorable Export Control Status
